issues.legal_issue: A conveyance of family properties by branches acting as separate joint-family units to an entity owned only by those branches can effect a division in status.
material_facts: Each of the eight sons described himself in the conveyance as acting for himself and as karta of the joint family consisting of himself and his descendants.
The conveyances transferred the properties to a company consisting only of the sons and their descendants.
The court found that the family had become divided in status before the conveyances or, at the latest, by the conveyances, after which the members dealt with the property as co-tenants.
issues.conclusion: The family was divided in status before the conveyances or, at the latest, by the conveyances themselves.
issues.legal_principle: A division in status may be established by the effect and terms of a transaction even if it is not formally a family settlement; a transaction transferring property from the larger family to an entity comprising the separate branches may disrupt the joint status and leave the members holding as co-tenants.

predicates.family_property_status_is_disputed: The parties dispute whether property is held by a joint family or by separated members.
predicates.branches_act_as_separate_joint_family_un: Members of the family execute the transaction in their capacities as representatives of separate joint-family units comprising themselves and their descendants.
predicates.family_property_is_transferred_to_an_ent: Family property is transferred to an entity whose ownership is confined to the family branches participating in the transaction.

issues.definition: When family property status is disputed, separate-family-unit conduct and a transfer to an entity owned only by those units result in severance of family status by the transaction.

issues.legal_issue: An alienation unanimously made by adult coparceners to preserve family property and benefit the family binds all coparceners even if the family remains joint.
material_facts: All eight sons and the adult coparceners of their branches joined in the transactions after joint deliberations and by unanimous decision.
The properties were transferred to a company of which the eight sons were the only shareholders, and the branches received equal shares.
The unchallenged evidence was that the purpose was to preserve the properties for family members and prevent any member from selling or mortgaging a share.
The court found that the transaction did not dissipate the property and was for the benefit of the family.
issues.conclusion: The transactions were for the benefit of the family and bound all coparceners, even if a joint family was still in existence.
issues.legal_principle: Under the principle stated in Hunooman Persaud v. Musummat Baboose, a manager may alienate joint-family property for legal necessity or the benefit of the estate so as to bind adult and minor coparceners. Whether a transaction benefits the family depends on its facts; it need not be defensive in character if a prudent owner or trustee would have undertaken it. Bal Mukand v. Kamla Vati supports assessing family benefit in light of the circumstances and the benefit conferred or reasonably expected when the transaction was made.

predicates.challenge_to_joint_family_property_alien: A proceeding challenges an alienation of property alleged to belong to a joint family.
predicates.adult_coparceners_unanimously_approve_af: All adult coparceners join in the transaction after deliberation and unanimously approve it.
predicates.alienation_is_intended_to_preserve_famil: The transaction is undertaken to protect or preserve the property for the family.
predicates.alienation_prevents_individual_dissipati: The transaction is intended to prevent an individual family member from disposing of or encumbering a share of the property.
predicates.property_is_not_dissipated: The transaction preserves the property rather than wasting or dissipating it.

issues.definition: A challenged joint-family property alienation binds all coparceners when the adult coparceners unanimously approve it after deliberation and it preserves the property, prevents individual dissipation, and does not dissipate the estate.

issues.legal_issue: An appeal may rely on evidence supporting a previously pleaded denial of joint-family status without raising a new plea.
material_facts: The written statement had specifically denied the alleged continuing joint family and alleged that the coparcenary had been disrupted before the relevant conveyances.
The appeal relied on the conveyance documents to establish that separation had occurred by the time of the transactions.
The court noted that the appeal had also challenged the finding that the family members remained joint.
issues.conclusion: The contention that the family had become divided was not a new point and could be considered on appeal.
issues.legal_principle: A contention is not a new plea when it is supported by a position specifically advanced in the pleadings; evidence may be relied on to establish when the pleaded disruption occurred.

predicates.appeal_challenges_a_finding_of_continued: An appeal disputes a finding that a family continued to hold property as a joint family.
predicates.pleadings_specifically_allege_prior_disr: The pleadings specifically deny continued joint status and allege an earlier disruption of the coparcenary.
predicates.appellate_evidence_supports_the_pleaded_: Evidence relied on in the appeal supports the alleged disruption and helps establish when it occurred.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges continued joint status, relies on a disruption specifically pleaded earlier, and supports that allegation with evidence, reliance on the evidence is not a new plea.
